newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria detains ex-minister over bombs, papers say.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria detains ex-minister over bombs, papers say.

text.p: A former Nigerian finance minister has been detained by police in connection with recent bomb blasts in Lagos, local newspapers reported on Saturday.

They said 59-year-old Olu Falae, a leading member of the opposition NADECO group, was invited to Lagos by the police from his hometown Akure in southwestern Nigeria on Thursday and has since been detained.
Police have not commented on the detention but friends and family of Falae said he was being held over the bomb attacks and denied that he was involved in any way.

"This country is our home. We have children and we are not going to do anything to jeopardise their future," said Falae's wife Rachel in the independent Guardian newspaper. "He is not guilty of what they are alleging."
Four bombs have rocked Lagos since November. In the latest attack on an army bus this week two soldiers were killed and about 30 others wounded.
Police said the explosion in November was a bungled one in which agents of the exiled opposition whom they blame for the blasts were killed on their way to plant bombs at Lagos airport.
They alleged that Falae's name was found in the diary of one of the dead would-be bombers, Nelson Kazim, who also allegedly visited the former finance minister.
But his wife countered this, saying "The name of the person whom Kazim visited was Falaye and not Falae."
Friends of Falae said in a statement on Friday that he was being wrongly accused.

"There is all indication that the authorities want to exploit the situation arising from the bombings to deal with perceived opponents even if they are innocent," they said in the statement reported in Thisday newspaper.

Falae was chief secretary to the government of former military president General Ibrahim Babangida. He later became finance minister, a post he quit to vie unsuccessfully for nomination as a presidential candidate in 1993.
